                                  11                       Defendant.

                                  12          Before the Court is the Parties’ Joint Statement regarding Defendant’s production of
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   documents in this Song-Beverly dispute. Dkt. 36. To summarize, Plaintiff seeks expansive
                                  14   discovery directed to the Subject Vehicle as well as other vehicles of the same make and model
                                  15   suffering from the similar problems from all databases and all “agents” of Defendant. Defendant
                                  16   primarily objects on grounds of overbreadth and lack of proportionality, citing California Code of
                                  17   Civil Procedure (“Calif. C. Civ. Pro.”) § 871.26(h) which identifies documents to be produced in
                                  18   Song-Beverely actions in state court. Having considered the record before it and the relevant law,
                                  19   including Calif. C. Civ. Pro. § 871.26 and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (“Fed. R. Civ. Proc.”)
                                  20   26 and 34, the Court determines that this matter may resolved without oral argument.
                                  21   Civ. L.R. 7-1(b).
                                  22          In this action, Plaintiff’s requests are impermissibly vast (e.g., RFP 1: “All DOCUMENTS
                                  23   regarding the SUBJECT VEHICLE that are maintained in YOUR databases.” Dkt. 36-3) and
                                  24   Defendant’s position statements impermissibly conclusory, (e.g., in re RFP 1: FCA US has
                                  25   complied in full with this Request and produced all responsive documents within its possession,
                                  26   custody or control,” followed by a lengthy list of documents without identifying to what any
                                  27   particular document pertains. Id.) As a result, it is not judicially efficient to review and rule on
                                  28   each disputed request individually. Accordingly, the Court ORDERS as follows:
                                         Case 5:24-cv-06870-BLF           Document 38         Filed 02/23/26      Page 2 of 4




                                   1      1. No later than February 26, 2026, the Parties are to meet and confer in good faith

                                   2          pursuant to the guidance provided by this Court below to resolve all outstanding

                                   3          production issues;

                                   4      2. No later than 12 p.m. on March 4, 2026, any remaining issues are to be submitted in

                                   5          accordance with this Court’s standing order;

                                   6      3. On March 10, 2026, at 10 a.m., the Court will hold an in-person discovery hearing on

                                   7          remaining issues. Counsel appearing must have full authority to negotiate and

                                   8          compromise and must be prepared to remain at Court the entire business day to

                                   9          engage in further meet and confer as ordered by the Court.

                                  10          The Parties’ meet and confer as ORDERED at step 1 above is to be conducted with the

                                  11   following guidelines in mind:

                                  12      •   Definitions. Plaintiff’s proffered “Defect Definition,” excluding categories (5) and (6),
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13          and the proffered “Engine Defect” definition are acceptable for meet and confer purposes

                                  14          to resolve the outstanding disputes.

                                  15      •   Calif. C. Civ. Pro. § 871.26. This legislation provides for an early and relatively broad

                                  16          disclosure of documents by plaintiffs and defendants in Song-Beverly actions, to be

                                  17          followed by mediation. While not an exclusive list of all documents to be produced in a

                                  18          case and not binding on this Court, the Court does find that the California legislation

                                  19          facilitates more efficient litigation of these matters and is a helpful guide to the relevant

                                  20          and proportional discovery required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(b)(1).

                                  21                 Any production of documents listed in Calif. C. Civ. Pro. § 871.26(h) or the

                                  22          categories of documents listed on page 10 of the Joint Statement, including “[A] list or

                                  23          compilation of customer complaints in Defendant’s electronically stored information

                                  24          database that are substantially similar to the alleged defect claim by Plaintiff, in vehicles

                                  25          purchased in California for the same year, make and model of the Subject Vehicle (e.g.,

                                  26          Customer Assistance Inquiry Records database search)” must include keys to all codes and

                                  27          abbreviations such that the content of each document is clear and comprehensible. Such

                                  28          productions must also be complete. Narrative summaries are acceptable. However, where
                                                                                         2
                                          Case 5:24-cv-06870-BLF              Document 38         Filed 02/23/26     Page 3 of 4




                                   1              a narrative is indicated, the absence of a narrative or narrative summary requires either

                                   2              further production or an affirmative, verified, statement that the narrative was searched for

                                   3              and not found.

                                   4          •   Custody and Control.” A keystone issue is whether Defendant has “control” over

                                   5              documents held by its authorized dealerships who, in this case, sold or leased and serviced

                                   6              the Subject Vehicle. Neither Party addresses this point adequately, instead making only

                                   7              conclusory statements: Plaintiff in a footnote citing only a general principle of agency;

                                   8              Defendant referring to “independent authorized sales and service” facilities. Dkt. 36 at 3,

                                   9              fn. 3 and at 10, respectively. Notably, Defendant does not state unequivocally that it does

                                  10              not have “custody or control” over documents held by its authorized dealers and concedes

                                  11              that it produced the “Retail Installment Sales Contract obtained from an independently

                                  12              owned and operated authorized sales facility regarding the Subject Vehicle.” Dkt. 36-3 at
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13              6 (emphasis supplied).

                                  14                     For purposes of production, a party has sufficient “control” over documents held by

                                  15              another party if the first party has the legal right to obtain the documents from the second

                                  16              party upon demand. In re Citric Acid Litig., 191 F.3d 1090, 1107 (9th Cir. 1999).

                                  17              Accordingly, Defendant is to consider its position on this issue with care, and the Parties

                                  18              are to meet and confer regarding production of responsive documents held by the relevant

                                  19              authorized dealers. If Defendant maintains its position that such documents are not within

                                  20              its custody and control, it will have to support its position with a declaration from a client

                                  21              representative with personal knowledge, and as well as a declaration of counsel, that it is

                                  22              unable to direct the authorized dealerships to provide it with documents. The supporting

                                  23              declarations are to be filed on March 4, 2026 along with the supplemental joint

                                  24              submission ordered above.

                                   3          schedule.
